chunks: And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام:
About abdominal discomfort that affects a man while he is able to bear it: should he perform salat in that state, or should he not perform salat?
So he said: “If he can endure patiently, and does not fear rushing the salat because of it, then let him perform salat and be patient.”

key_terms.إِعْجَالًا: hastening or rushing in a way that affects proper prayer
key_terms.الْغَمْزِ: abdominal discomfort or internal pain affecting the person
key_terms.بَطْنِهِ: his stomach or abdomen, the place of the discomfort

ai.seo_question: Can a person pray while experiencing stomach pain if he is able to bear it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about performing salat while experiencing stomach discomfort. If the person can bear it and it will not cause him to hurry and compromise the prayer, he should pray and remain patient.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1061 - Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj asked Abu al-Hasan (as) about a man who feels discomfort in his stomach but is able to bear it.
He asked whether the man should continue praying in that situation or not.
Imam (as) replied: "If he can tolerate the pain and does not fear it causing him to rush the prayer, then he should pray and be patient."
